30 June
On this day in 1813

Raja Karam Singh became Maharaja of Patiala

Raja Karam succeeded Maharaja Sahib Singh at the age of 15. He helped the British in the conflict with the Gorkhas and was rewarded with 16 parganas (district sub-divisions) in Simla Hills as gifts.

30 June is remembered for an event of 1813: Raja Karam Singh became Maharaja of Patiala. It belongs to the period of The Sikh Empire of Maharaja Ranjit Singh (1799–1839).

Historical background

The Sikh Empire of Maharaja Ranjit Singh (1799–1839)

Ranjit Singh of the Sukerchakia misl took Lahore in 1799, was proclaimed Maharaja in 1801 and united the misls into a single state stretching from Peshawar and Kashmir to the Sutlej. He modernised the Khalsa army, gilded Sri Harmandir Sahib, and kept peace with the British under the Treaty of Amritsar (1809).

On this day in this period: 1813 Raja Karam Singh became Maharaja of Patiala.
